items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: And I think those examples: Ray Charles and Buddy Greco, kind of pointed me the way to piano.

ctx.x: What did you learn from watching those people?

Well that’s when I learned I’d probably have to play piano, because I saw Ray Charles come in and Buddy Greco came in and he said that he was making $1500 a week back in the forties with a hit record, and he gave it up to play piano with Benny Goodman for $150 a week. And he told me — he would take me out playing golf when people would invite him to the country club, so I’d go out and play golf with him. And he said, “What are you doing here? Why aren’t you back singing somewhere?” He didn’t want me being a house…
What about interacting with the audience. Did that come naturally for you, sort of — that’s a big part of being a singer and being able to be sort of a front man.
